note: R25: fourth hand-written set, final untouched test, written without access to the frozen test

stories.text: At the small radio station on Gullbrae Hill, the night presenter, Solveig, read the weather at ten. Her producer, Wojciech, had left a note on the desk because the second microphone was broken. Solveig borrowed a headset from the sports room and finished the show with it. When the morning team arrived, they found the note still taped to the desk.
qs: Who had left a note on the desk?
Where did Solveig borrow a headset from?
When did Solveig read the weather?

stories.text: A magpie named Corvo lived above a beekeeper's yard. One spring he wanted honey, but the bees would not let him near the hives. Corvo asked a slow old toad, Bembo, for advice, and the toad told him to bring the bees a gift of clover. The magpie flew to the far meadow and carried back three stems of clover in his beak. After that, the queen bee let him taste one drop of honey each evening.
qs: Who did Corvo ask for advice?
What did the toad tell Corvo to bring the bees?
How many stems of clover did Corvo carry back?
Who let Corvo taste the honey?

stories.text: The ferry left Pellmouth at seven with a crate of lemons on deck. Halfway across, a deckhand named Kodzo moved the crate into the cabin because spray was soaking it. At Dunmere the crate was carried off by a porter, who loaded it onto a mule cart. By noon the lemons were in the market at Dunmere, stacked beside the fish stalls.
qs: Where was the crate of lemons when the ferry left?
Who moved the crate into the cabin?
Why did Kodzo move the crate?
Who carried the crate off the ferry?
Where were the lemons by noon?

stories.text: Mrs Olatunji ran a tailor's shop on Kettle Street, and her apprentice, Florian, swept the floor each morning. On Monday a customer brought in a torn wedding jacket. Florian wanted to mend it himself, but Mrs Olatunji said the silk was too fine for a beginner. She sewed the sleeve while he pressed the trousers, and the jacket was ready by Wednesday.
qs: Who swept the floor each morning?
What did the customer bring in?
What did Florian do while Mrs Olatunji sewed the sleeve?

stories.text: In a dry valley, a hedgehog named Pim found a puddle after the storm. A proud crow landed beside it and said the water belonged to whoever saw it first. Pim pointed out that he had been drinking before the crow arrived. Just then a fox trotted up and drank half the puddle while they argued. The hedgehog and the crow shared what was left and never quarrelled about water again.
qs: What did Pim find after the storm?
Who said the water belonged to whoever saw it first?
When did Pim find the puddle?
What did the hedgehog and the crow do with what was left?

stories.text: At dawn the pickers met at the top of the Lessard vineyard. Their baskets were stacked by the stone wall, and the foreman, Ruy, handed them out. By eleven the baskets were full, so a tractor took them down to the press house. In the afternoon Ruy's daughter Ghislaine counted the grapes at the press house and wrote the total in a red book.
qs: Where did the pickers meet at dawn?
What took the baskets down to the press house?

stories.text: Every Friday a night market opens in the car park behind the library. Mei sells dumplings there from a blue stall, and her neighbour, an old man called Faruk, sells lamps. Last Friday the wind blew one of Faruk's lamps off his table. Mei caught it before it hit the ground, and Faruk gave her a small lamp to thank her.
qs: Where does the night market open?
What blew a lamp off Faruk's table?

stories.text: A young goat, Brisa, wanted to cross the river to eat the tall grass on the other side. The otter who lived under the bank offered to carry her on a log if she promised to share. Brisa promised, but on the far side she ate all the grass herself. The next week the river rose, and when Brisa asked for a ride home, the otter only laughed and swam away.
qs: Who wanted to cross the river?
What did the otter offer to carry her on?
What did Brisa do on the far side?

stories.text: Two climbers, Maren and Anselmo, reached the glacier hut late in the afternoon. Maren left her ice axe outside the door, but in the night snow buried it. In the morning the hut warden, a quiet woman named Gudrun, dug the axe out with a shovel. The climbers set off for the summit at six, and Anselmo carried the rope.
qs: Where did Maren leave her ice axe?
What did Gudrun dig the axe out with?

stories.text: The puppet theatre on Quince Row had only one dragon puppet, and it was kept in a trunk under the stage. Before the Saturday show, the puppeteer, Torgny, could not find it. His niece Liesl had borrowed the dragon to show her class, and she brought it back just as the curtain opened. Torgny was so relieved that he let her work the dragon's tail.
qs: Where was the dragon puppet kept?
Why had Liesl borrowed the dragon?
What did Torgny let Liesl work?

stories.text: A field mouse named Tilde stored seeds in an old boot at the edge of the farm. One cold morning a rat came and claimed the boot was his house. Tilde did not argue; she invited the rat in for breakfast instead. While they ate, the farmer's cat walked past, and the rat was glad the boot had a mouse inside to warn him. From then on the two shared the boot through the winter.
qs: Who claimed the boot was his house?
What did Tilde do instead of arguing?
What walked past while they ate?

stories.text: On Tuesday, Chiamaka took the early train from Varrow to visit her grandmother. She left her umbrella on the train, and a conductor named Mr Ilves put it in the lost property office at Ashgrove station. Chiamaka spent the afternoon with her grandmother baking bread. That evening she collected the umbrella from Ashgrove on her way home.
qs: Where did Chiamaka leave her umbrella?
Who put the umbrella in the lost property office?
Where was the umbrella in the afternoon?
What did Chiamaka do in the afternoon?

stories.text: A delivery van blocked Orchard Road for two hours on Thursday after its back wheel came off. The driver, Mr Wisniewski, was not hurt. A mechanic from the garage on Fell Street fitted a new wheel, while a police officer named Constable Ntuli directed the traffic. The road was open again before the school buses came.
qs: Who was the driver of the van?
How long was the road blocked?

stories.text: A lazy cat named Dumpling slept on the warm roof of a bakery. Every morning a sparrow woke him by singing on the chimney. One day Dumpling chased the sparrow away so he could sleep longer. The next morning no one woke him, and he slept through the moment when the baker threw out the broken pastries. A pigeon ate them all, and Dumpling went hungry until night.
qs: What did Dumpling do to the sparrow?
What did the baker throw out?

stories.text: The lighthouse keeper, Mr Thorvaldsen, kept a spare lantern in the boathouse. On Sunday morning his son Edvin rowed the lantern across to the island because the old lamp had cracked. By lunchtime the new lantern hung at the top of the lighthouse. Edvin rowed back in the evening with the cracked lamp in the bottom of the boat.
qs: Where was the spare lantern kept?
Who rowed the lantern across to the island?
Where was the new lantern by lunchtime?
What was in the bottom of the boat in the evening?
When did Edvin row the lantern across?

stories.text: Grandpa Sotiris promised to teach his granddaughter, Leni, how to fish. They waited on the jetty all morning and caught nothing. Leni grew bored and began to sketch the boats, and that was when her line tugged hard. She pulled in a silver mackerel, which Grandpa Sotiris cooked for supper.
qs: Who promised to teach Leni to fish?
Where did they wait all morning?
What did Leni begin to sketch?
What did Grandpa Sotiris do with the mackerel?

stories.text: A beaver named Brannoc built his dam faster than any beaver in the forest, but he never helped the others. When a flood broke his dam, he asked his neighbours to help him fix it. The old heron, who had watched him for years, told the beavers to help anyway. They rebuilt the dam in one night, and Brannoc spent the next summer mending everyone else's lodges.
qs: Who told the beavers to help anyway?
How long did it take to rebuild the dam?
What did Brannoc do the next summer?

stories.text: Before school, Laleh put her library book in her bag. At break she lent it to her friend Shinpei, who read it under the oak tree in the playground. After lunch Shinpei left it on his desk, and the teacher, Mrs Sjoberg, put it on the shelf by the window. Laleh found it there at home time.
qs: Where was the book before school?
Who had the book at break?
Where did Shinpei read the book?
Who put the book on the shelf?
Where was the book at home time?

stories.text: The beekeeper, Mr Tavares, wore a white suit and a net over his face. On Saturday his neighbour's dog knocked over one of the hives in the yard. Mr Tavares calmed the bees with smoke and lifted the hive back onto its stand. The neighbour, Mrs Quinlan, brought him a lemon cake to say sorry.
qs: What knocked over one of the hives?
How did Mr Tavares calm the bees?
What did Mrs Quinlan bring him?
When did the dog knock over the hive?

stories.text: A crab and a gull lived on the same rock. The gull, Merel, liked to boast about flying, and the crab, Ludo, liked to boast about his shell. One afternoon a storm blew Merel into a crack in the rock where she could not open her wings. Ludo crawled into the crack and pushed her out with his claws. After that, the gull never laughed at the crab's slow walk.
qs: Who liked to boast about flying?
What did Ludo like to boast about?
What blew Merel into a crack?
Where did the storm blow Merel?
What did Ludo push her out with?

stories.text: Mr Obiora drove his van of pumpkins from the farm to the town square on Saturday morning. Halfway there he stopped at a petrol station, where a boy named Teo bought two pumpkins. In the square Mr Obiora sold the rest by noon. He drove home through the hills and reached the farm just after dark.
qs: What was in Mr Obiora's van?
Where did Mr Obiora stop halfway?
When had Mr Obiora sold the rest?
When did he reach the farm?

stories.text: Dr Nwosu, the village vet, was called to a farm at midnight because a cow was having a calf. The farmer, Bertil, held a torch while she worked. The calf was born just before one o'clock, and Bertil's children named it Pepper. In the morning Dr Nwosu had breakfast at the farmhouse before she drove back to her clinic.
qs: What did Bertil's children name the calf?
Where did Dr Nwosu have breakfast?

stories.text: A young owl named Hollis could not stay awake at night like the other owls. She asked a bat what to do, and the bat told her to sleep through the bright afternoon. Hollis tried it, but the noisy squirrels in her tree kept waking her. In the end a badger let her sleep in his quiet burrow, and she hunted all night with her brothers.
qs: Who could not stay awake at night?
Who told Hollis to sleep through the afternoon?
Who let Hollis sleep in his burrow?
What did Hollis do all night?

stories.text: At eight the caretaker, Mr Delacroix, unlocked the museum and hung the key on a hook in the office. At ten a guide named Devika took the key to open the map room. She forgot to return it and carried it in her pocket all day. When the museum closed, Mr Delacroix found the key in Devika's coat, which was hanging in the staff room.
qs: Where was the key at nine?
Who took the key at ten?
Why did Devika take the key?
Where was the key when the museum closed?

stories.text: Firefighters rescued a kitten from the roof of the Moravec bakery on Tuesday. The kitten, which belongs to the baker's son, Matyas, had climbed up a drainpipe. A ladder was raised by the crew, and firefighter Leah Strand carried the kitten down in a basket. Matyas gave the crew a tray of cinnamon buns.
qs: What did Matyas give the crew?
Where was the kitten rescued from?

stories.text: A squirrel named Nutmeg hid acorns in twenty places around the pond, but she forgot where most of them were. A jay, who had watched her, offered to tell her the places in return for half the acorns. Nutmeg agreed, and they dug up eighteen acorns together. In spring the two acorns they missed grew into small oak trees.
qs: Who hid acorns around the pond?
How many places did Nutmeg hide acorns in?
Who offered to tell Nutmeg the places?
What did the jay want in return?
What did the missed acorns grow into?

stories.text: Lars and his sister Bozena took the morning ferry to Tarnholm Island with a picnic basket. They left the basket in the shade of a pine tree while they swam. A goat wandered over and ate their sandwiches. In the afternoon they bought fish soup at a cafe by the pier, and they caught the last ferry home at six.
qs: Where did they leave the picnic basket?
Where did they buy fish soup?
When did they catch the last ferry home?

stories.text: Mrs Quaresma, the school librarian, ordered forty new books in September. They arrived in two boxes, but one box was sent to the wrong school by mistake. A driver named Fiifi brought the missing box back a week later. The pupils helped Mrs Quaresma put stickers on every book before the reading fair.
qs: How many new books did Mrs Quaresma order?
Who brought the missing box back?
Where was one box sent by mistake?
What did the pupils put on every book?

stories.text: A peacock named Amadou spent every morning admiring his tail in the pond. A plain brown hen, Clementine, spent her mornings scratching for worms. When winter came, the peacock had nothing stored, but the hen had a pile of dry seeds under the barn. Clementine shared the seeds, and Amadou kept her warm under his wide tail on the coldest nights.
qs: Who admired his tail in the pond?
Where did the hen keep her seeds?
What did Amadou do on the coldest nights?

stories.text: Seung-woo cycled from his flat to the bakery at seven to buy rolls. He locked his bicycle to a lamppost outside, but when he came out a tyre was flat. He wheeled the bicycle to Mr Petrakis's repair shop on the corner. While the tyre was being fixed, Seung-woo ate two rolls on the bench outside, and he rode home at half past eight.
qs: Where did Seung-woo cycle at seven?
Where did Seung-woo lock his bicycle?
Whose repair shop did Seung-woo take the bicycle to?
Where did Seung-woo eat two rolls?

stories.text: In the tax office on the third floor, a clerk named Zubair kept a fern on his windowsill. When he went on holiday, his colleague Marguerite watered it every Monday. The fern grew so big that the manager, Mr Aaltonen, asked to move it to the meeting room. Zubair came back and found his fern at the end of the long table.
qs: What did Zubair keep on his windowsill?
Who asked to move the fern?
Where was the fern when Zubair came back?
When did Marguerite water the fern?

stories.text: Two ants, Kip and Marlo, found a strawberry too heavy to carry. Kip wanted to call the whole nest, but Marlo wanted to keep it secret. While they argued, a beetle rolled the strawberry down the hill. Marlo ran home to fetch help, and twenty ants carried it back up before sunset.
qs: Who wanted to call the whole nest?
Who wanted to keep the strawberry secret?
What rolled the strawberry down the hill?
How many ants carried the strawberry back up?
When did the ants carry the strawberry back up?

stories.text: A tour bus left the Brightwater Hotel at nine with a guide named Mrs Ocampo. The group spent the morning at the salt mine and had lunch in a village called Rennick. One tourist, Mr Haugen, left his camera at the restaurant. The driver went back for it while the others visited the cathedral, and the bus returned to the hotel at five.
qs: Where did the group spend the morning?
What did Mr Haugen leave at the restaurant?
Who went back for the camera?
What did the others do while the driver went back?

stories.text: The cook at the Heron Inn, Rocio, burned the soup on a busy Saturday. Her assistant, a tall boy called Ikenna, ran to the market for more onions. While he was gone, Rocio made a bean stew instead, and the guests liked it so much that it went on the menu.
qs: What did Ikenna go to the market for?

stories.text: A mole named Grig dug a tunnel under the garden fence to reach the carrots. The rabbit, who owned the carrot patch, was angry at first. Then Grig showed her that the tunnel led straight to the stream, where the water was clean. The rabbit let him eat one carrot a day, and she used his tunnel to fetch water.
qs: Who dug a tunnel under the garden fence?
How many carrots could Grig eat a day?
What did the rabbit use the tunnel for?

stories.text: A parcel for Mrs Villalobos was left on the wrong doorstep on Monday. Her neighbour, Ibrahim, took it inside to keep it dry. On Tuesday Ibrahim's daughter carried the parcel across the street to Mrs Villalobos's porch. Mrs Villalobos opened it that evening and found the wool she had ordered.
qs: Who carried the parcel across the street?
Where was the parcel on Tuesday evening?

stories.text: Every spring the gardeners of Brackenfield Allotments hold a contest for the longest bean. This year a retired pilot, Mr Brennan, won with a bean as long as his arm. The judge, Mrs Kaur, measured it twice to be sure. His prize was a new watering can, which he gave to the youngest gardener, a girl named Ragnhild.
qs: How many times did Mrs Kaur measure the bean?
Who did Mr Brennan give the prize to?

stories.text: A fox cub called Rasko found a shiny bottle cap and thought it was a gold coin. He hid it under a stone and guarded it for three days without hunting. A weasel told him the cap was worthless, so Rasko, who was very hungry by then, went back to hunting. The next morning a crow stole the cap, but Rasko only laughed.
qs: What did Rasko think the cap was?
Where did Rasko hide the cap?
Who told Rasko the cap was worthless?

stories.text: On the school trip, Mr Abiodun carried the first-aid kit in his rucksack. At the waterfall he gave it to a parent, Mrs Yamada, because he had to go back for a lost glove. Mrs Yamada used a plaster from the kit when a boy named Sorin cut his knee on a rock. By the time the group reached the car park, the kit was back in Mr Abiodun's rucksack.
qs: Who had the first-aid kit after Mr Abiodun gave it away?
Why did Mr Abiodun go back?
What did Mrs Yamada use from the kit?
Where was the kit when the group reached the car park?

stories.text: The violinist, Wiebke, left her violin backstage at the concert hall after the rehearsal on Friday. A stagehand named Bogdan locked it in the instrument cupboard for the night. On Saturday morning Wiebke could not find it and was very worried. Bogdan arrived at ten with the key, and the concert began on time that evening.
qs: When did Wiebke leave her violin backstage?
Where did Wiebke leave her violin?
Who locked the violin in the cupboard?
Where was the violin on Friday night?
When did Bogdan arrive with the key?
